root_cause.text: The macb PCI glue driver unregistered the clocks before unregistering the platform device, causing a use-after-free when platform_device_unregister triggers a runtime resume callback that accesses the already-freed clock structures.
root_cause.evidence: The KASAN report shows the use-after-free in clk_prepare called from macb_runtime_resume during platform_device_unregister, while the clocks were freed by clk_unregister in macb_remove before that point. The patch fixes this by saving the clock pointers locally and calling clk_unregister after platform_device_unregister.

    net: macb: Added PCI wrapper for Platform Driver.
    
    There are hardware PCI implementations of Cadence GEM network
    controller. This patch will allow to use such hardware with reuse of
    existing Platform Driver.
    
    Signed-off-by: Bartosz Folta <bfolta@cadence.com>
    Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/drivers/net
bic_trace_step.reason: In macb_remove(), after calling platform_device_unregister(plat_dev), the code accesses plat_data via dev_get_platdata(&plat_dev->dev). At that point, the platform device may have been freed, making plat_data a dangling pointer. Then clk_unregister(plat_data->pclk) and clk_unregister(plat_data->hclk) cause a use-after-free. The clock unregistration should be performed before the platform device is unregistered to avoid this issue.
